value.assumption_check: The load-bearing assumption is that hermes' skill and memory objects map onto (content, vector, provenance) without loss. Measured: its skills are SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter (name, description, version, author, license, platforms, prerequisites, metadata) and its memories are MEMORY.md / USER.md chunks — both LOOK like content with provenance. Not measured: whether the frontmatter carries anything that is neither content nor provenance and would be dropped silently. The falsifier is written so a loss routes to two honest stores rather than to a quiet flattening.
value.builder_check: (1) THERE IS ALMOST NOTHING TO BUILD and a builder should be told so explicitly, because the reflex on a ticket like this is to write a wrapper. nexus_table, deposit_learning, counsel and propose all already take owner. (2) VECTORS ARE THE CALLER'S: tree.py's own note says vectors arrive as DATA and the embed call goes out through inference_domain. So the work is the MAPPING from a hermes skill/memory to (content, vector, provenance), and nothing else. (3) THE REAL RISK is scope: do not build a sync daemon, do not mirror ~/.hermes, do not poll. A deposit happens when hermes learns, event-driven, or it does not happen. (4) DEPENDS on the hermes device ticket for there to be a hermes at all — this reads queued on it.
value.collision_check: Checked whether Law 6 permits a non-CC owner of a corpus: it does, and cleanly — ownership gates writes to STATE, hermes would gate its own, and tree.py holds no state of its own to gate. That is the Law's own test being PASSED, not an exception carved. No collision found. A distinction worth recording: this is the first time the tools rung's owner-as-call-parameter design serves an owner that is not CC, which is a claim tree.py's charter makes and nothing has yet tested.
value.falsifier_check: Stands and is cheap to check: a hermes-authored learning retrievable by counsel under owner='hermes', readable by CC without attaching to hermes' process. HORIZON: the first hermes learning deposit. Wrong-intent tell is written and is the important half — if the mapping distorts hermes' shape, the honest answer is TWO stores that agree and say so, never one store that flattens the other and calls it integration.
value.missing_check: Yes, one: WHICH NEXUS. The intent says owner='hermes' and never says what nexus name its learnings deposit under. tree.py's verbs take both, and the existing nexi (orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate) are the chart's. My read, not ratified: hermes gets its own nexus names rather than depositing into the chart's, because a chart nexus is the memory of how CHART STAGES decide, and a second agent's learnings are not that. Recorded so the builder does not quietly pick one.

value.better_approach: Let it keep ~/.hermes and mirror the contents into the trees — rejected, and by a precedent from this very system: inference_domain deliberately CUT spend from its trail rather than carry it in two places, because one number in two records is a number that can drift. Two records of one learning is the same defect with a longer fuse.
value.hidden_assumption: That hermes' skill and memory objects map onto (content, vector, provenance) without loss. Unverified — measured only that its skills are SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter and its memories are MEMORY.md / USER.md chunks, both of which LOOK like content with provenance. Whether the mapping is lossless is the first thing to test, and the falsifier is written so that a loss routes to two honest stores rather than to a quiet flattening.
value.prior_art: cairn/tools/tree/tree.py, whose charter states outright that `owner` is a CALL PARAMETER, that the tool holds no corpus and addresses whichever corpus its caller owns, and that this IS the proof of what 'a tool has users, not an owner' means in code (Akien, 2026-08-13). This intent is that design meeting its first non-CC caller — prior art so exact that the intent is mostly an act of USING it.
value.real_collision: None. The nearest question is whether Law 6 even permits hermes to own a corpus: it does, and cleanly — ownership gates writes to STATE, hermes would gate its own, and tree.py has no state of its own to gate. That is the Law's own test being passed, not an exception being carved.
